prompt:
12-second portrait gameplay explainer for Meowdoku! Use the supplied image as the exact first frame. Preserve this same game's pastel art, exact 8×8 colored grid, all region boundaries, three fish lives, 0/8 counter, three rule cards and Download button. Locked continuous front view; no cuts, zoom crop, board motion or new controls.
Rule: one cat per row, column and color region; cats cannot touch, even diagonally. The verified first cell is row 1, column 6, counted from top-left. It is a separate single purple region, not part of neighboring green.
0–2.5s: establish the empty board and existing hand over r1c6.
2.5–4.5s: the hand makes a quick double-tap on r1c6, two contacts close together on that same cell, no drag or swap. Give each contact a small touch ring.
4.5–7s: the second tap reveals exactly one cat centered within r1c6, with springy squash-and-stretch and a tiny paw sparkle. Counter changes once from 0/8 to 1/8. All three fish remain.
7–9.5s: hold the first placement in presentation slow motion; cat blinks or twitches an ear as the local glow settles. A brief rule-card edge glint may emphasize the narration without changing its text.
9.5–12s: hand idles and sparkles clear. End with one cat and 1/8. All other cells retain their initial state. No exclusion crosses, duplicate cats, recoloring, automatic extra moves, later tutorial step, life loss, reward or victory.
Strong but compact game feel: two crisp taps, elastic cat pop, warm cell-local rim light and short paw/star sparks. Keep all text and colors legible. Sync two soft clicks, a friendly mew and warm confirmation chime. Sparse playful plucked music stays beneath clear English narration, exactly: "Double-tap to place a cat. One per row, column, and color. Keep cats apart." No added subtitles or win fanfare; keep the complete grid and HUD visible.
